original.title: Truth and Method
original.note: Library record's first publication year is 2004; 1975 is the edition or translation cited here.

core_idea: Understanding is interpretation. We grasp a text, action or person by moving between part and whole (the hermeneutic circle), and always from within our own historical horizon; understanding happens when the interpreter's horizon and that of the text meet.
key_concepts_note: Use the concepts already stored for this theory in the library (theories.concepts).
when_to_use: Interpreting texts, documents, policies or interview accounts in depth.
Studies where the researcher's own pre-understanding is part of the analysis.
Typical designs: hermeneutic text analysis, narrative analysis, hermeneutic phenomenology.
common_mistakes: Treating the hermeneutic circle as a step-by-step technique.
Hiding the researcher's pre-understanding instead of working with it.
